## Triage result — task 10426 / issue #6061

**Verdict: design-only; ready for the design stage.** Revalidated on 2026-11-05: #6061 is OPEN with no hard-stop labels. Parent design #6019 and consumer design #6026 are OPEN; #6043 is CLOSED by merged PR #6269. GitHub search returned no matching open PR for the storage-growth/retention design. This is not a runtime defect: no reproduction, code change, or code tests apply. #6061 itself is the design handoff, so no duplicate queue task is needed.

**Evidence and bounded route:** the current Atlas sizing document is a point-in-time baseline, not the requested churn/retention model: 107,639 chunks, 3,072 raw bytes/vector, 4.8 GB total, and 1.15 GB in `messages` ([baseline](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/cf2d06702e79a54857acb1266a2091b79df2d54c/doc/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision.md#L21-L24)). The same inventory measures a 160,576 B/row vector-index shadow (~17.3 GB), with the projected database at ~22.1 GB against 24 GB included (~1.9 GB headroom); validate that unusual amplification rather than assuming it applies to future versions ([C1](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/cf2d06702e79a54857acb1266a2091b79df2d54c/doc/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision.md#L136-L147)). The staging design permits unlimited detail before promotion and archives closed staging databases, but does not specify archive expiry; model this lifecycle separately from retained corpus versions ([staging](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/cf2d06702e79a54857acb1266a2091b79df2d54c/doc/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision.md#L215-L243)).

Design #6061 around measured per-source new/changed bytes per period × retained-version duration, adjusted for span reuse, manifests/metadata, index amplification, and hot/cold storage. Use the per-batch ledger in [#6058](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6058) as the calibration source; it will take weeks of operation to provide representative rates, so define the model and calibration procedure now but keep initial defaults conservative (retain more) until data matures. Project against #6019's plan envelope and include staging archives separately. Coordinate the retention inputs with [#6026](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6026) and its [#6041](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6041) dry-run rule-engine work; keep cold-tier movement ahead of any deletion by at least one full retention cycle. The merged [#6043 decision record](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/cf2d06702e79a54857acb1266a2091b79df2d54c/doc/2026-11-05T15-50-41Z_decision_atlas_pitr_vs_retention/2026-11-05T15-50-41Z_decision_atlas_pitr_vs_retention.md#L39-L53) confirms retention requires both a named trigger and a class rule; PITR is not a substitute. Coordinate delta/reuse assumptions with [#6028](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6028).

The remaining blocker is only *measured recalibration*: representative ledger observations need to accrue. No destructive retention action should be enabled as part of this design triage.
